speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin evaluating your 8-month-old son's feeding difficulties and abdominal distension, could you please describe his bowel movement patterns and stool consistency? Also, has he had any episodes of vomiting or visible blood in his stool?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: His fussiness and tenderness to touch suggest significant abdominal pain, so I need to assess for signs of obstruction or severe inflammation. Has he passed any gas or stool in the last 24 hours, and does he have a fever?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to check for specific signs of bowel obstruction or malrotation. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel segments with an airless rectum strongly suggest a distal obstruction, such as Hirschsprung disease or meconium ileus. Have you noticed if his initial meconium stool was delayed in passing after birth, or has he ever required rectal examinations or enemas to pass stool?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of abnormal stool passage and abdominal distension, combined with the X-ray findings, is highly suggestive of Hirschsprung disease. I will now request a contrast enema to visualize the transition zone and confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Contrast_Enema

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease

speaker: Doctor
text: The contrast enema confirms a transition zone in the distal colon, which is diagnostic for Hirschsprung disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
